SELECT
  t.boroname,
  COUNT(t.tree_id) AS tree_count,
  AVG(it.Estimate_Mean_income) AS average_mean_income
FROM modern_data.main.trees AS t
JOIN
  modern_data.main.income_trees AS it
  ON t.zipcode

content.text: I will now construct the SQL query. I will join the `trees` and `income_trees` tables using an `INNER JOIN` on their common `zipcode` column. Then, I will filter the results to include only entries where both the median and mean income are positive and a borough name is present. Following that, I will group the data by borough to compute the total tree count and the average mean income. Finally, I'll sort the boroughs based on the tree count in descending order and select the top three.

args.sql:
SELECT
  t.boroname,
  COUNT(t.tree_id) AS tree_count,
  AVG(it.Estimate_Mean_income) AS average_mean_income
FROM modern_data.main.trees AS t
JOIN
  modern_data.main.income_trees AS it
  ON t.zipcode = it.zipcode
WHERE
  it.Estimate_Median_income > 0 AND it.Estimate_Mean_income > 0 AND t.boroname IS NOT NULL AND t.boroname <> ''
GROUP BY
  t.boroname
ORDER BY
  tree_count DESC
LIMIT 3;
